description: 《Like a Prayer》描寫一段充滿神祕、激情與心靈渴望的情感體驗，巧妙結合宗教信仰與愛情的意象。歌中的主角感到生命充滿未知與孤獨，但每當聽見對方呼喚自己的名字，便彷彿得到安慰與救贖，感受到如同回家般的溫暖。她將這份強烈的吸引力比喻為祈禱，透過天使、天堂與唱詩班等意象，表達愛情與神聖力量交織的感受。歌曲亦流露出對親密、自由與精神昇華的渴望。最終，《Like a Prayer》傳達的是愛、信仰與自我探索之間的深刻連結：當情感與靈性相互交融，人便可能在強烈的感動中超越孤獨，找到心靈的慰藉與歸屬。

vocabulary.usage: 當某件事的原因或答案還不清楚，令人想知道真相時，可以用 mystery。
vocabulary.prompt: 哪一句正確使用了「mystery」來表示「謎」？
options: Please put two mysteries in my coffee. I like it sweet.
The sign says this road is a mystery, so cars must drive backward.
The train is a mystery because it has six doors.
Nobody knows who took the cake. It is a mystery.
optionExplanations: mystery 不是可以加進咖啡的糖；可說 Please put two spoons of sugar in my coffee.
mystery 不表示交通規則，也不能據此要求車輛倒退；可說 The sign says cars must turn left.
火車有六扇門不等於存在謎團；若只描述車門，可說 The train has six doors.
不知道誰拿走蛋糕，答案未明，因此可以說 It is a mystery.
vocabulary.explanation: 不知道誰拿走蛋糕，答案未明，因此可以說 It is a mystery.

vocabulary.meaning: 獨自站著；獨自面對某件事。
vocabulary.usage: 表示一個人沒有別人陪伴，或必須靠自己面對事情時，可以用 stand alone。原歌詞也有較抽象的「獨自面對人生」之意。
vocabulary.prompt: 哪一句正確使用了「stand alone」？
options: Even when her friends left, Mia was brave enough to stand alone.
The hotel can stand alone only after it gets a driver's license.
The shoes stand alone because they forgot how to walk together.
I stand alone my lunch when the table is full.
optionExplanations: 即使朋友離開，Mia 仍勇敢地獨自面對，符合片語意思。
飯店不是司機，不需要駕照才能「獨自站著」；可說 The hotel is next to the station.
鞋子不會因為忘記一起走路而自行行走；若要說鞋子放在門旁，可說 The shoes are by the door.
stand alone 不能直接接 my lunch 當成「吃午餐」的動詞；可說 I eat lunch alone.
vocabulary.explanation: 即使朋友離開，Mia 仍勇敢地獨自面對，符合片語意思。

vocabulary.usage: 想請別人直接喊出自己的名字，或描述聽見有人叫自己時使用。
vocabulary.prompt: 哪一句正確使用了「call my name」？
options: I call my name in the oven until the bread is ready.
If you need me, just call my name and I will come.
We call my name at five dollars, but the shop wants ten.
The map calls my name because it wants to know my address.
optionExplanations: call my name 是呼喊名字，不是烤麵包的方法；可說 I put the bread in the oven.
需要我時就喊我的名字，我便會過來，用法自然。
call my name 不是商品的價格；可說 The shop wants ten dollars.
地圖不會主動呼喚名字或詢問住址；可說 The map shows my street.
vocabulary.explanation: 需要我時就喊我的名字，我便會過來，用法自然。

vocabulary.meaning: 感覺像家一樣；令人安心、自在。
vocabulary.usage: 一個地方或與某人相處時，讓你感到熟悉、溫暖、安全，可以說 feel(s) like home。
vocabulary.prompt: 哪一句正確使用了「feels like home」？
options: This chair feels like home because it has a roof and two windows.
My new school feels like home because everyone is kind to me.
The airport feels like home because every plane pays the rent.
I feel like home the door before I leave.
optionExplanations: 椅子有屋頂與窗戶並不是此片語的意思；可說 This chair is comfortable.
同學與老師很友善，讓新學校有家的感覺，使用正確。
飛機不會向機場繳房租；feel like home 說的是熟悉或安心的感受，不是租屋關係。
feel like home 不能直接當成「關門」的動詞；可說 I close the door before I leave.
vocabulary.explanation: 同學與老師很友善，讓新學校有家的感覺，使用正確。

vocabulary.usage: 描述跪下的姿勢，例如找東西、清理地板或祈禱時，可以用 on my knees。
vocabulary.prompt: 哪一句正確使用了「on my knees」？
options: My computer is on my knees because it has lost its legs.
The calendar is on my knees because Friday needs a place to sit.
I got down on my knees to look under the bed.
I bought three on my knees at the market.
optionExplanations: 電腦不會因為失去腿而跪下；若電腦放在膝上，可說 My laptop is on my lap. 注意 lap（大腿上方）和 knees（膝蓋）並不相同。
星期五不需要坐位，on my knees 也不表示日曆上的一天；可說 Friday is on my calendar.
跪下來查看床底，正確描述身體姿勢。
on my knees 是姿勢片語，不是市場裡可以買三個的商品；可說 I bought three apples at the market.
vocabulary.explanation: 跪下來查看床底，正確描述身體姿勢。

vocabulary.usage: 表示一天結束、下一天開始的時間，可用 midnight。
options: The clock says midnight because it is too shy to say twelve.
Midnight is the name of the soup when it is very cold.
The library closes at midnight, so we must leave before twelve.
I midnight my room every Sunday to make it clean.
optionExplanations: 時鐘不會因為害羞而改口；midnight 的意思就是午夜十二點。
midnight 是時間，不是冷湯的名稱；可說 The soup is cold.
圖書館在午夜十二點關門，時間與用法皆正確。
midnight 不是打掃房間的動詞；可說 I clean my room every Sunday.
vocabulary.explanation: 圖書館在午夜十二點關門，時間與用法皆正確。

vocabulary.usage: 因疲倦、難過、放心或無奈而深深呼出一口氣時，可以用 sigh。
options: He gave a long sigh when he saw all the work on his desk.
The menu sighed because nobody ordered the expensive page.
Please sigh the door after you come in.
I put a sigh in the box and sent it to my cousin.
optionExplanations: 看見桌上大量工作而長嘆一口氣，是 sigh 的自然用法。
菜單不會因為顧客沒點餐而嘆氣；可說 Nobody ordered the expensive dish.
sigh 不是「關門」；可說 Please close the door after you come in.
嘆息不是能裝箱寄送的實體物品；可說 I put a gift in the box and sent it to my cousin.
vocabulary.explanation: 看見桌上大量工作而長嘆一口氣，是 sigh 的自然用法。

vocabulary.meaning: 掌握情況；能控制或管理某事。
vocabulary.usage: 說某人能決定事情如何進行，或能妥善處理情況時，可用 in control。
vocabulary.prompt: 哪一句正確使用了「in control」？
options: My jacket is in control of Tuesday, but only after lunch.
The pilot stayed calm and was in control of the plane.
The pencil is in control because it has written its own rules.
I in control a letter to my uncle yesterday.
optionExplanations: 外套不會管理星期二；這裡把抽象的控制權硬套在衣服與日期上。
飛行員保持冷靜並掌控飛機，正確使用 in control of。
鉛筆不會自行制定規則；可以說 I use a pencil to write the rules.
in control 不是「寫信」的動詞；可說 I wrote a letter to my uncle yesterday.
vocabulary.explanation: 飛行員保持冷靜並掌控飛機，正確使用 in control of。

vocabulary.usage: 一群人一起唱歌，尤其在學校、教堂或正式演出時，可以用 choir。
options: The choir sang three songs at the school concert.
My bicycle joined the choir because its bell has a nice voice.
We use a choir to open the door when we lose the key.
I need a choir of milk for this cake.
optionExplanations: 合唱團在學校音樂會上演唱三首歌，用法正確。

vocabulary.usage: 當某人的真實個性、身分或情況與第一印象不同時，可以說 You are not what you seem. 對事物則可說 It is not what it seems.
vocabulary.prompt: 哪一句正確使用了「not what you seem」？
options: You are not what you seem because your photo is two inches tall.
I am not what you seem the windows every morning.

You looked unfriendly at first, but you are very kind. You are not what you seem.
optionExplanations: 照片的大小不能直接證明一個人的真實個性與表象不同；可說 Your photo is two inches tall.
這個片語不能充當「擦窗戶」的動詞；可說 I clean the windows every morning.
說三明治時不能用指向人的 you seem；若真要說某物與外表不同，應使用 It is not what it seems.
